text:
alex: deploy-bot alert: canary group 'autoscale-v2' reporting elevated 5xx and flapping readiness checks. rolling canary = 20% today. paging oncall.

oncall-bot: @here oncall page triggered by 5xx-rate-high (rule: canary-5xx > 2% sustained 2m). Priority: P1. Incident channel created.

maya: I see 3.8% 5xx on the canary lb, spikes line up with scale events. healthcheck failures on /healthz returning 503 intermittently.

chris: confirmed from logs: timeout to model-runtime on a subset of pods right after scale-up. stack trace shows 'kv-cache-miss' and backlog.

sre_lead: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout/stop traffic to canary 2) revert feature flag 3) scale warm pool 4) collect heap/metrics. Who can flip the flag?

alex: i'm on it. pausing via rollout controller now.

deploy-bot: rollout pause acknowledged for deployment/llm-api-canary (revision=57).

alex: flipping kill-switch flag: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"canary_new_autoscaler","value":false}'` -> response 200 OK

maya: good. routing shows traffic draining. 5xx trending down from 3.8% -> 1.1% in last 30s.

chris: also increasing warm pool: `kubectl scale deployment llm-runtime-warm --replicas=8 -n inference` — doing that now.

sre_lead: logs to grab: runtime logs from pods that failed, kube events during scale, and autoscaler decision logs. Collecting into /tmp/canary-3333.tar.gz

alex: grabbed traces and a small heap profile. attaching snippet of recent error lines:
```
2026-03-15T10:52:03Z llm-runtime[pod-az2-7fdf]: ERROR request_id=abc123 timeout waiting for kv-cache response
2026-03-15T10:52:04Z llm-runtime[pod-az2-9f12]: WARN readiness probe failed: 503 Service Unavailable
2026-03-15T10:52:08Z autoscaler[controller]: scaled deployment llm-runtime from 2 -> 6 replicas (policy=scale-up)
```

maya: looks like scale-up caused concurrent cold starts hitting shared disk/cache; we need to tune concurrency limits for autoscaler or add a jitter/warmup.

chris: quick customer impact note: based on sampling, ~0.9% of production requests routed through canary saw higher latency or 5xx during the window. No large customer-facing outage detected, but some tail errors.

oncall-bot: Handoff: current oncall alex -> night oncall maya at 11:00. Recorded mitigation steps.

alex: i'm marking the incident 'mitigated' — rollout paused, flag reverted, warm pool scaled. next actions: postmortem runbook item to add warmup hook and autoscaler cooldown, add stronger readiness gating.

sre_lead: agree. Maya will pick up tracking and open a follow-up ticket for quantifying warmup metrics + canary gating thresholds.

maya: noted, creating ticket INF-5873 with impact summary and suggested remediation.

chris: leaving a short note for support: "Some customers may have seen transient 5xx during a canary scale-up. Root cause: autoscaler-induced cold starts interacting with shared KV cache. Rollout paused and feature flag reverted." plz send to CS.

alex: pinging cs@redwood: draft sent. reactions: :thumbsup: :fire:

pagerduty: Incident P1 closed (acknowledged -> resolved). Resolution: paused rollout + roll back flag. No follow-up on-call escalation.

sre_lead: closing notes: keep an eye on the next canary after we apply warmup changes. If 5xx rate >1% re-open incident. thanks team.
__notes: generated for dataset: contains root message and chronological replies, includes bots and on-call handoff. No title field per agents.md.
